scope: Internal reduced-order model only. These are engineering assumptions and numerical experiments, not measured Tesla Roadster specifications.
protocol: 120 Hz; level floor; x=0,z=-80; settle 3 s; set initial forward speed; no steering, suction, jets, collisions, or reset. Stop threshold <=0.1 m/s, followed by >=1 s of four-wheel hold <=0.15 m/s. Body collision invalidates a brake stop. The averageDecelerationUntilStop field excludes the 1 s hold; observation averages include it.

findings.friction: Each ray wheel load is max(0,k*(rest-length)-c*v_normal)/alignment; each contact has capacity mu*normalLoad. Combined longitudinal and lateral force is radially saturated to that friction circle. Tire force is applied at the ray hit point, so actual pitch and load transfer arise in the rigid body.
findings.braking: Explicit brake requests +/- brakeForce/contactCount per wheel, regularized as -v_long*(mass/contactCount)*28 near zero. It is not brake disc torque, wheel inertia, a slip-ratio tire curve, or a physical ABS implementation.
findings.acceleratorRelease: With no brake and no accelerator, regeneration is bounded by min(2600 N,60000 W/speed); aerodynamic drag and body damping add a small deceleration. At 100 km/h this means approximately 2160 N of regenerative force, not 42000 N of brake demand.
findings.brakeThrottleConflict: In the measured legacy model, throttle adds motor force during explicit braking. At high speed braking authority is reduced; near zero motor force and the velocity regularization reach a nonzero creep equilibrium. Brake priority should suppress drive torque and booster demand when braking deliberately.
findings.suspension: The legacy displayed wheel length is clamped at 0.08 m but the force law uses the unbounded geometric length. This can hide an already overcompressed physical state. A compressed-wheel collision envelope and progressive bump stop should enforce the same geometry used by the visible wheel and wheel arch.
findings.assumptions: mu=1.25 is an assumed high-grip dry tire/road value, not Tesla calibration. Treat 0.85 and wet-road values as sensitivity cases. Raising mu to hide input conflicts would be physically misleading.
limitations: Single-ray wheels do not model tire width, finite contact patches or sidewall/curb impacts.
Wheel angular speed is visual kinematics; rotational wheel inertia, ABS pressure cycling, tire relaxation and load sensitivity are absent.
No official Roadster braking/adhesion calibration is inferred from these tests.
No driver reaction time is included; these are pure brake-application distances.
